text: The wattle bush was gold in fading light.
Sunny pattered softly down the path.
And there upon a twig, a tiny bird,
in feathers blue as pieces of the sky.
A fairy-wren! No bigger than a plum,
with a tail that flicked and bounced with every hop.
“Hello!” he chirped. “I'm rounding up my family!
We sleep together, snug as garden peas!”
His little family fluttered from the bushes,
brown and blue, they gathered on the branch.
They shuffled close together in a row,
each one snuggled up against the next.
“The secret to warm dreams,” the wren explained,
“is sharing them with everyone you love.”
He hopped into the middle of the row,
the brightest bead upon a cosy string.
Their feathers fluffed together in the dusk,
till no one could tell where one wren stopped.
The row of little birds began to sway,
rocked gently by the evening's quiet breathing.
Sunny nestled down beneath their branch,
warmed through by all the closeness up above.
The wattle hushed. The garden held its breath.
Everything was peaceful, snug, and safe.
Her eyes grew heavy under sleeping wrens.
One slow blink… then another… then no more.
And Sunny slept beneath the row of blue,
dreaming warm and close and never lonely.
Goodnight, Sunny. Goodnight, fairy-wrens.
Goodnight, gold wattle. Goodnight, little one.
